descripcion: At B2 the goal is to fix the most common verb-noun collocations of everyday and simple professional English: make a decision, take a risk, have an effect. These are not interchangeable with do or take at random — each noun has its own fixed partner.

ejemplos.texto: We need to make a decision by tomorrow.
It's worth taking the risk, in my opinion.
The change had a big effect on the whole team.

notas: These verbs aren't interchangeable: to do a decision or to make a risk both sound wrong to a native speaker.
Have is the default verb for many abstract nouns: have an effect, have an impact, have a problem.
Make an effort is one of the most common collocations in everyday spoken English.

contraste.es: Spanish tomar covers several of these collocations (tomar una decisión – make a decision, tomar un riesgo – take a risk), which English splits between make and take. That single difference explains most confusion between the two verbs.
contraste.de: German machen leads to make a photo (ein Foto machen) where English says take a photo, and eine Entscheidung treffen gives no clue that English uses make. The make/take split has to be learned pair by pair.
contraste.it: Italian fare leads to make a photo (fare una foto) where English says take, and prendere un caffè to take a coffee where English says have. The make/take/have split has to be learned pair by pair.
contraste.fr: French faire leads to make a photo (faire une photo) where English says take, and prendre un café to take a coffee where English says have. The make/take/have split has to be learned pair by pair.
contraste.pt: Portuguese tirar uma foto corresponds well to take a photo, but tomar um café leads to take a coffee where English says have. The make/take/have split has to be learned pair by pair.

errores: Using do as a default verb for every collocation.
Saying make a risk instead of take a risk.
Saying do an effort instead of make an effort.
autochequeo: Have I chosen the right verb for each noun, not defaulted to do?
Have I used make and take correctly, not interchangeably?
Does the combination sound natural to a native speaker?
Have I used at least four different collocations?
Have I avoided do as a catch-all verb?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on verb-noun collocations. Mark each one and give the correct verb where it's wrong, especially confusions between make, do, take and have. Do not rewrite the text.
